messages:
alex: Starting playback run for a 2h production slice (anon, sampled). got some nondet perf diffs vs live. need triage.

maria: Can you paste the harness command and sampling params?

alex: `./playback --slice=srv-10-2026-03-15 --anon=pbkdf2 --sample-rate=0.5 --seed=42 --kv-warmup=true --kernel-policy=auto` got ~7% higher p95 token latency on dedicated-gpu compared to live.

kevin: Did you pin kernels? auto can pick aten->cutlass depending on seq len distribution. try `--kernel-policy=explicit:cutlass` and `explicit:aten` for apples-to-apples.

jordan: Also check KV cache behavior: if the live traffic had warmed KV per-session and playback replays interleaved sessions, parity breaks. Use session-affinity sampling or replay session order.

alex: Good point. current replay flattens session boundaries to preserve anonymity. That might explain the warmup mismatch.

maria: For anonymization we use pbkdf2 with per-session salt so session ids are distinct but relative ordering is kept if we don't shuffle. Are we shuffling? if yes, set `--shuffle=false`.

alex: We did `--shuffle=true` earlier to reduce burstiness. I'll rerun with shuffle=false and seed=1337.

perf-bot: harness-run 1728004321: started at 1728004321, samples=12k, threads=64, batch_policy=dynamic, kv_warmup=on

kevin: When comparing kernels, also match batching heuristics: dynamic batching thresholds (max_batch_tokens / latency_slo) can differ. Document the batch histogram from live and force the same histogram in playback using `--batch-sim=historical`.

alex: Ran both kernel pins + shuffle=false + batch-sim historische. Results:
- aten: p50 12ms, p95 48ms
- cutlass: p50 11ms, p95 44ms
Now parity delta reduced to ~1.2%.

jordan: Nice. Still >0 — any quantization path differences? check fused-kernel flags and FP16 fallback rates.

maria: Also verify KV cache hit ratio. I instrumented a cheap counter: `kv_hits/kv_lookups` during playback. In the failing run it was 0.62 vs live 0.79.

alex: Aha. Lower kv hit explains increased token decode latency due to more memory loads. Hypothesis: sampling shuffle introduced fake session boundaries causing cache misses.

kevin: For deterministic parity you need:
1) deterministic RNG seed
2) preserved session ordering or a replay-preserving-affinity mode
3) identical kernel + quantization flags
4) identical batching policy (batch size distribution)

maria: Suggest adding a `--replay-preserve-affinity` mode that rehydrates anonymized session ids into consistent buckets without exposing real ids.

alex: Implemented a prototype: maps anon-session -> consistent bucket via salted hash + stable RNG seed. rerun yields kv_hit 0.78 and p95 within 0.4% of live.

perf-bot: harness-run 1728004321: finished at 1728004870, delta_p95=0.4%, kv_hit=0.78, kernels=explicit:cutlass

jordan: Great. Next steps: add a checklist for apples-to-apples runs in docs, include explicit flags we toggled, and record perf profiles (nvprof + runtime traces) for any >1% delta.

maria: I'll open a short PR with `--replay-preserve-affinity` docs and add a small test in replay-harness CI that runs a tiny slice and asserts kv_hit >= 0.75 when shuffle=false.

alex: thanks. saved the run artifacts under s3://redwood-playback/1728004321/ and uploaded profile tarball.

kevin: Also log kernel selection trace in the harness output (seq_len, selected_kernel) so we can aggregate and spot policy flips.

alex: done. i've added `--dump-kernel-trace=stdout` and posted a short sample in the run artifact.

maria: nice. close loop: once PR is up ping #eng-runtime and mark as experimental in release notes.

alex: will do. :thumbsup:
